summary: The streets here are named for the world — Naples, Vienna, Madrid, Prague, Munich, Athens, Lisbon, Edinburgh — and for twenty years after 1917 the Board did little in this district but grade them, kerb them and lay their pavements, one at a time. In 1917 it took land for a drainage alley running from London Street through to Mission. In 1928 it let the Druids of Green Valley Grove No. 145 hold a masquerade ball at Corinthian Hall on Mission Street, and licensed two petrol stations, at Mission and Avalon and at Geneva and Naples.
